title: Bandleaders watering down his difficult arrangements
summary: Bandleaders such as Highland told him they had to cut his arrangements because commercial bands lacked time to perfect them; Swinging Cats was only played passably.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: an arrangement. A lot of my arrangements, that I have very few that I've had to play -- now, this is really on the up and up -- very few bands I have had to really play what I write, without -- let's say, well, if -- I'm not a drinking man, but I imagine if you get ahold of some beverages, and they're so strong you would dilute it with something, with either water or pop or something to keep it from being so strong? You know?

Well, that's what they would have to do, even when I was with Highland. Well, Highland told me. He says, "Zilner, your arrangements are fine. But we'll have to cut here and chop here, because it takes us too long, having a commercial band, to get the arrangements down. We'll have to put too much time in perfecting them.
Yeah, you were quite -- I was listening to Swinging Cats today.
And that last chorus is tricky.
"Swinging Cats," yeah. Well, I wished it could have been really played. It really wasn't played right. I wish it could have been just really played.
